items.front: IVC mature (urban) phase dates, and which metal it did NOT know?
items.back: Mature phase c. 2600–1900 BCE (NCERT); a Bronze/Chalcolithic culture — iron was unknown.

items.front: Four phases of the Harappan culture in order?
items.back: Pre-Harappan → Early Harappan → Mature Harappan → Late Harappan.

items.front: Who announced the IVC to the world (1924), and who first surveyed Harappa's robbed bricks?
items.back: John Marshall announced it in 1924; Alexander Cunningham (first ASI DG) noted it earlier.
Daya Ram Sahni — Harappa (1920–21); Rakhaldas Banerjee — Mohenjo-daro (1921–22).

items.front: Four cardinal boundary sites of the IVC (N-E-W-S)?
items.back: North Manda (Chenab), East Alamgirpur, West Sutkagendor, South Daimabad. Mnemonic MASD.

items.front: The Great Bath is found at which single site?
items.back: Only at Mohenjo-daro — a watertight tank on the citadel. (Never Harappa — classic trap.)

items.front: Dholavira: location, water feature, UNESCO status?
items.back: Khadir island, Rann of Kutch (Gujarat); cascading stone reservoirs ('jala durga'); UNESCO 2021, India's 40th.
Lothal: tidal dockyard, bead factory, sole port, early rice. Kalibangan: ploughed field, fire altars.
A craft town (beads, shell, seals, weights) with NO citadel; <7 ha vs Mohenjo-daro's ~125 ha.

items.front: Harappan seals: material, script direction, decipherment?
items.back: Mostly steatite; pictographic script written right-to-left; ~375–400 signs; still undeciphered.

items.front: Harappan weights: material, shape, number system?
items.back: Chert, cubical, unmarked; lower range binary (1–32), higher decimal (multiples of 16). Bricks 4:2:1.

items.front: Mesopotamian trade names: Meluhha, Dilmun, Magan?
items.back: Meluhha = Indus region; Dilmun = Bahrain; Magan = Oman (copper source). Barter, maritime.

items.front: Dancing Girl vs 'Priest-King' — material and site?
items.back: Dancing Girl: bronze (cire perdue, tribhanga). Priest-King: steatite/stone, trefoil shawl. Both Mohenjo-daro.

items.front: Late Harappan phase dates and hallmark of decline?
items.back: c. 1900–1300 BCE; seals, script, standard weights and long-distance trade fade — de-urbanisation with continuity.
